chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the meats of the bukh (strutting/racing) camels and their milks, so he said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat and drinking the milk of bukh camels?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'bukh' camels, a specific breed known for their racing or strutting gait, affirming the permissibility of consuming both their meat and milk. It highlights the Shia scholarly approach of distinguishing between the physical characteristics or utility of an animal and its ritual purity, confirming that such camels are not inherently impure or prohibited like the camel of the tribe of Thamud.
